A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the participatory practices in these four cities are not yet sufficiently embedded in the local political and administrative structures.

, although the four cities under investigation have been using a variety of participatory practices, the latter have failed to build a democratic capacity in the sense that they have not been able to create a democratic culture and to foster a democratic attitude among citizens.
the four case studies provide us with an opportunity to observe the different ways in which public participation is used to build the capacity of the democratic process in the local self-governance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to contribute to the development of democratic capacity of a given municipality, the practice of public participation needs to be supported by a number of factors.
the current literature on public participation and participatory democracy has to be further developed, as it fails to capture the complexity of the phenomenon.

, despite the fact that the cities under investigation differ in terms of their democratic capacity and the level of their citizens’ engagement in public affairs, participatory projects have the capacity to build democratic capacity in the long run, by providing citizens with a sense of empowerment, by making them aware of their rights and by giving them a voice.
